title: LaMET-Agent: An Agent Framework for Large-Momentum Effective Theory Analysis
summary: Large-momentum effective theory (LaMET) provides a first-principles framework for computing the $x$ dependence of light-cone parton distributions from lattice QCD. Over the past decade, theoretical and numerical advances have established a mature multi-stage workflow for systematic calculation of parton physics, although its implementation still requires expert judgment and substantial repeated effort. We present lamet-agent, an open-source large language model (LLM) agent framework that organizes this workflow into an executable, reproducible, and inspectable analysis pipeline. The present release supports collinear quark distributions and implements correlator analysis, renormalization, Fourier transformation, perturbative matching, continuum, physical pion mass and infinite-momentum extrapolations, and automated result review. We validate it on four end-to-end analyses: pion parton distribution functions in the gauge-invariant and Coulomb-gauge formulations, and pion and kaon distribution amplitudes, obtaining results consistent with the published calculations. Extensions to transverse-momentum-dependent distributions, generalized transverse-momentum-dependent distributions, and gluonic distribution functions are planned for subsequent releases.

AI.tldr: An open-source LLM agent, lamet-agent, has been developed to streamline the workflow for computing parton distributions from lattice QCD using Large-momentum effective theory (LaMET), with validation on pion and kaon distribution analyses.
AI.motivation: To address the need for a systematic, reproducible, and less labor-intensive approach to calculating parton physics using LaMET, while maintaining the ability to conduct expert-level judgment and analysis.
AI.method: Development of an open-source framework, lamet-agent, which automates key steps in the calculation of parton distributions, including correlator analysis, renormalization, Fourier transformation, perturbative matching, and various extrapolations. The tool is validated through comparison with published results for pion and kaon distributions.
AI.result: lamet-agent successfully reproduces existing calculations for pion parton distribution functions and pion and kaon distribution amplitudes, demonstrating its effectiveness and reliability as a computational tool in this field. Future releases will expand its capabilities to other types of distributions.
AI.conclusion: The introduction of lamet-agent marks a significant step towards more accessible, automated, and efficient computation of parton distributions within the LaMET framework, enhancing both productivity and the potential for new discoveries in lattice QCD.

title: Measuring Mass Splittings in Baryon SU(2) Multiplets
comment: Proceedings for The 43rd International Symposium on Lattice Field Theory (Lattice 2026)
summary: The inclusion of isospin-breaking corrections arising from electromagnetic interactions and the up-down quark mass difference is becoming increasingly important in lattice QCD calculations, as the precision of observables is at or approaching the percent level. In this context, the RM123 method has been employed in recent years to take into account such isospin corrections. In this work, we study baryon mass splittings using the RM123 approach. Preliminary results are presented for the mass splittings within spin-1/2 and spin-3/2 baryon SU(2) multiplets, obtained using twisted-mass ensembles tuned close to physical quark masses. We consider only valence contributions, with the splittings computed at leading order in the isospin-breaking parameters.

AI.tldr: This paper explores the use of the RM123 method to incorporate isospin-breaking corrections in lattice QCD calculations, specifically focusing on baryon mass splittings. Preliminary results are provided for mass differences within certain baryon multiplets, using ensembles with quark masses near physical values and considering only leading order effects from isospin breaking.
AI.motivation: As the accuracy of observables in lattice QCD calculations reaches or approaches the percent level, it becomes essential to include isospin-breaking corrections due to electromagnetic interactions and the difference in up-down quark masses. The motivation here is to improve the precision of theoretical predictions by accounting for these corrections, which can have a significant impact at such high levels of accuracy.
AI.method: The researchers utilize the RM123 approach to study baryon mass splittings. They employ twisted-mass ensembles that are fine-tuned to be close to the actual quark masses found in nature. This study is limited to valence quark contributions and calculates the splittings to leading order in the parameters responsible for isospin breaking.
AI.result: Preliminary findings are reported for the mass splittings within spin-1/2 and spin-3/2 baryon SU(2) multiplets. These results provide insight into how isospin-breaking effects influence the predicted mass differences between baryons in the same multiplet.
AI.conclusion: The application of the RM123 method to baryon mass splittings has yielded initial results, suggesting that isospin-breaking corrections can be effectively computed and contribute to the refinement of lattice QCD predictions. Further work will likely aim to extend this analysis to higher orders and possibly include sea quark contributions.

title: The Peskin-Takeuchi $S$ parameter and vector meson decay constants in $N_f=8$ QCD
summary: We use lattice gauge theory to investigate the Peskin-Takeuchi S parameter in SU(3) gauge theory with eight light fundamental fermions (eight-flavor QCD), a candidate for walking technicolor. We develop a new approach to computing S using the first time moment of current correlators, in addition to the conventional vacuum-polarization method, and obtain consistent results. Finite-volume (FV) corrections are estimated using data at multiple lattice volumes and a formula motivated by chiral perturbation theory. At the smallest fermion mass, the one-doublet contribution is S = 0.281(5)(17), smaller than the value $\sim 0.35$ in scaled-up 2+1-flavor QCD (without subtracting the SM contribution). However, contrary to naive expectations, S toward smaller fermion masses is not necessarily suppressed once FV corrections are included. The resulting Gasser-Leutwyler parameter $L_{10}^r(M_ρ)$ is similar to that in real-world QCD. We also determine the vector and axial-vector meson decay constants, $F_ρ$ and $F_{a_1}$. The ratio $F_ρ/F_π$ is stable against the fermion mass and consistent with the KSRF estimate, implying a $ρππ$ coupling similar to that in real-world QCD. We predict the techni-rho decay width into weak bosons to be $Γ_ρ/M_ρ\lesssim 0.24/N$, where N is the number of weak doublets. We further find that the rho- and $a_1$-dominated Weinberg spectral-function and Das-Mathur-Okubo sum rules are satisfied, yielding S and $L_{10}^r(M_ρ)$ consistent with our main results. We discuss implications for BSM model building.

title: Multilevel Plaquette-Space Sampling for Lattice Gauge Theories with Local Constraint Solves
comment: 9 pages main text, 38 pages total, 10 figures, 9 tables
summary: Lattice gauge theories are an important class of physical models with high-dimensional structured distributions that underpin first-principles calculations in particle, nuclear, and condensed-matter physics. Recent advances in generative modeling have opened new avenues for sampling Boltzmann distributions in lattice gauge theories, offering the potential to alleviate limitations of traditional Monte Carlo methods, including critical slowing down and topological freezing. However, generative samplers for lattice gauge theories are typically constructed in link space, where correlations become increasingly long-ranged toward weak coupling, posing a challenge for learning. Plaquettes provide a more natural representation, as the action is local in these variables. However, exact Bianchi constraints restrict them to a lower-dimensional manifold, complicating direct generative modeling. We introduce a multilevel normalizing-flow construction that samples directly in plaquette space while satisfying these constraints exactly. The key idea is a coarse-to fine factorization that transforms a globally coupled constraint problem into a sequence of local solves: at each refinement, every determined plaquette depends on at most four newly generated variables, while the size of the constraint problem remains independent of the lattice size. We validate the construction for $U(1)$ in two and four dimensions and for $SU(2)$ in two dimensions. Our multilevel Plaquette-Space Sampler (PSS) substantially outperforms link-space baselines, with the advantage increasing toward weak coupling, where the gauge coupling becomes small. This regime is particularly challenging for generative sampling and, in asymptotically free gauge theories, is relevant to continuum studies.

AI.tldr: A novel multilevel normalizing-flow construction, the Plaquette-Space Sampler (PSS), is introduced to sample in plaquette space for lattice gauge theories, which outperforms traditional link-space methods, especially in the weak coupling regime.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to improve upon existing generative sampling techniques for lattice gauge theories, which are crucial for first-principles calculations in physics. Traditional Monte Carlo methods suffer from critical slowing down and topological freezing, while current generative samplers face challenges with long-range correlations in link space. The PSS aims to address these issues by directly sampling in a more natural representation, the plaquette space, while satisfying Bianchi constraints exactly.
AI.method: The method involves a multilevel normalizing-flow construction that allows for direct sampling in plaquette space. It utilizes a coarse-to-fine factorization approach, transforming a globally coupled constraint problem into a sequence of local solves, thereby simplifying the learning process. This technique ensures that each determined plaquette depends on at most four newly generated variables, regardless of the lattice size.
AI.result: The results show that the Plaquette-Space Sampler (PSS) performs significantly better than the link-space baselines, particularly as the system approaches the weak coupling limit, where the gauge coupling is small. The PSS was validated for U(1) in 2D and 4D, and SU(2) in 2D, demonstrating its effectiveness in overcoming the limitations of previous methods in this challenging regime.
AI.conclusion: The conclusion drawn from the study is that the multilevel Plaquette-Space Sampler (PSS) is an effective method for generative sampling in lattice gauge theories, offering improved performance over traditional link-space sampling, especially in the context of weak coupling. This advance has the potential to enhance first-principles calculations in particle, nuclear, and condensed-matter physics.
